svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate — OSV checks dependencies where their owner can fix them
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: OSV checks dependencies where their owner can fix them
Framework tools are checked in the toolbox
Project dependencies still block the project

g.text: Given every framework tool in a generated project contains the same
vulnerable package
Every shipped tool receives the same vulnerable lodash lockfile in a disposable project. The
saved public advisory lets the real scanner work offline.
When the generated project's OSV scan leaves inherited tools to the
toolbox
OSV finds no project dependency to check. Inherited tools do not block the generated
project, even when the project adds its own scanner arguments.
Then the toolbox's OSV scan reports the same vulnerable framework tools
The toolbox's own base config reports the same vulnerable package in every shipped tool. The
exclusion only belongs to generated projects.
When the developer adds vulnerable dependencies in project-owned
locations
The developer adds the same package at the repository root, in a custom tool, in a similarly
named tool, and in a nested .config directory. None of these locations belongs to the
framework.
Then OSV reports every project-owned copy of the vulnerable package
OSV reports all four project dependencies. The inherited copies remain excluded, so a
blanket .config exclusion or a package-name exemption cannot pass this check.
When the developer updates the framework through Copier
Copier advances the disposable project's toolbox release. The project's scanner arguments
and custom tool files survive the update.
Then OSV keeps the same ownership boundary after the update
The same scan reports the same four project dependencies after the update. The generated
base arguments still exclude framework tools.
When the developer removes the project dependency fixtures
The developer removes the four disposable project lockfiles. Only inherited framework
dependencies remain.
Then the project's empty OSV scan passes with a clear result
OSV reports "No package sources found" and "No issues found". MegaLinter passes: an empty
project scan succeeds without an error diagnostic.
